---
title: "Shiny app"
author: "Jeremy Fyrer"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---
```{r}
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD CLEANED DATA
# ============================================================

athletes <- read_csv(
  "athletes_clean.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

medals <- athletes %>%
  filter(!is.na(Medal))

country_data <- medals %>%
  distinct(
    NOC, Country, Games, Season,
    Year, Event, Medal
  )

athlete_data <- medals %>%
  distinct(ID, Name, Games, Event, Medal)

# ============================================================
# 2. CREATE SUMMARY DATA
# ============================================================

country_summary <- country_data %>%
  group_by(Country, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    Gold = sum(Medal == "Gold"),
    Silver = sum(Medal == "Silver"),
    Bronze = sum(Medal == "Bronze"),
    Total = Gold + Silver + Bronze,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

athlete_summary <- athlete_data %>%
  group_by(ID, Name) %>%
  summarise(
    Gold = sum(Medal == "Gold"),
    Silver = sum(Medal == "Silver"),
    Bronze = sum(Medal == "Bronze"),
    Total = Gold + Silver + Bronze,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

gender_data <- athletes %>%
  distinct(ID, Year, Season, Sex) %>%
  group_by(Year, Season, Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    Participants = n_distinct(ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

country_trends <- country_data %>%
  group_by(Country, Year, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    Medals = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ============================================================
# 3. USER INTERFACE
# ============================================================

ui <- navbarPage(

  title = "Olympic History Dashboard",

  header = tags$div(
    style = "background-color:#17365D;
             color:white;
             padding:20px;",
    h2("120 Years of Olympic History"),
    p("Interactive analysis of Olympic athletes,
      countries, medals and participation (1896-2016)")
  ),
 # HOMEPAGE
  tabPanel(
    "Home",

    tags$style(HTML("
      .home-page {
        background-color: #f4f6f9;
        padding: 30px;
        color: #243247;
      }

      .hero {
        background: linear-gradient(135deg, #17365D, #28527A);
        color: white;
        padding: 55px 35px;
        border-radius: 12px;
        text-align: center;
        margin-bottom: 25px;
      }

      .hero h1 {
        font-size: 38px;
        font-weight: bold;
        margin-bottom: 15px;
      }

      .hero p {
        font-size: 17px;
        max-width: 800px;
        margin: auto;
        line-height: 1.7;
      }

      .home-card {
        background: white;
        padding: 25px;
        border-radius: 10px;
        margin-bottom: 20px;
        border-left: 5px solid #D4A017;
        box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.07);
        height: 100%;
      }

      .home-card h3 {
        color: #17365D;
        font-weight: bold;
        margin-top: 0;
      }

      .credits {
        background-color: #17365D;
        color: white;
        padding: 25px;
        border-radius: 10px;
        text-align: center;
        margin-top: 20px;
      }

      .credits h3 {
        color: #E6C56B;
      }

      .credits p {
        line-height: 1.7;
      }

      .home-section-title {
        color: #17365D;
        font-weight: bold;
        margin-top: 30px;
        margin-bottom: 18px;
      }
    ")),

    div(
      class = "home-page",

      # HERO SECTION
      div(
        class = "hero",
        h1("120 Years of Olympic History"),
        p(
          "Exploring more than a century of Olympic competition through data, 
          visualization, and historical analysis."
        ),
        br(),
        p(
          "From the first modern Olympic Games in 1896 to Rio 2016, 
          discover how athletes, countries, and the Olympic movement 
          have changed over time."
        )
      ),

      # PROJECT INTRODUCTION
      h2(
        "About the Project",
        class = "home-section-title"
      ),

      p(
        style = "font-size:16px; line-height:1.8;",
        "The Olympic Games are one of the world's most recognized 
        sporting events, bringing together athletes from across the 
        globe. However, the history of the Games tells a much larger 
        story than athletic achievement alone. It reflects changes 
        in international participation, gender representation, 
        national success, and the role of sport in society."
      ),

      p(
        style = "font-size:16px; line-height:1.8;",
        "This interactive project uses historical Olympic athlete 
        and medal data to explore those developments. Through 
        interactive graphs, comparisons, and tables, visitors can 
        examine Olympic history from different perspectives and 
        discover patterns across more than 120 years of competition."
      ),

      # PROJECT GOALS
      h2(
        "Our Goals",
        class = "home-section-title"
      ),

      fluidRow(
        column(
          4,
          div(
            class = "home-card",
            h3("Explore Olympic Success"),
            p(
              "Examine medal counts across countries and athletes 
              to identify historic performances and the most 
              decorated competitors."
            )
          )
        ),

        column(
          4,
          div(
            class = "home-card",
            h3("Understand Participation"),
            p(
              "Investigate how Olympic participation has evolved, 
              particularly the changing representation of men and 
              women throughout the history of the Games."
            )
          )
        ),

        column(
          4,
          div(
            class = "home-card",
            h3("Investigate Historical Trends"),
            p(
              "Explore how age, national performance, and the 
              advantage of hosting the Olympic Games have changed 
              across different eras."
            )
          )
        )
      ),

      # PUBLIC VALUE
      h2(
        "Why This Project Matters",
        class = "home-section-title"
      ),

      div(
        class = "home-card",
        p(
          style = "font-size:16px; line-height:1.8;",
          "We hope this project makes Olympic history more accessible 
          to students, educators, sports fans, and the general public. 
          By turning a large historical dataset into interactive 
          visualizations, visitors can explore information that might 
          otherwise be difficult to interpret."
        ),
        p(
          style = "font-size:16px; line-height:1.8;",
          "The dashboard encourages curiosity and data-driven thinking. 
          It allows users to compare countries, recognize changes in 
          gender participation, investigate the relationship between 
          hosting and athletic success, and better understand how the 
          Olympic Games have developed over time."
        )
      ),

      # HOW TO USE THE DASHBOARD
      h2(
        "Explore the Dashboard",
        class = "home-section-title"
      ),

      div(
        class = "home-card",
        p(
          "Use the tabs above to explore the different parts of 
          the project. Each section offers interactive graphs, 
          filters, or tables that allow you to investigate 
          Olympic history at your own pace."
        ),
        tags$ul(
          tags$li("Country Medals – Compare medal totals by country."),
          tags$li("Top Athletes – Explore the most decorated athletes."),
          tags$li("Age & Performance – Examine athlete age and medal outcomes."),
          tags$li("Hosting Advantage – Compare medal performance at home and away."),
          tags$li("Gender Participation – Track participation by gender over time."),
          tags$li("Country Trends – Follow national medal performance across Olympic years.")
        )
      ),

      # AUTHORS AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
      div(
        class = "credits",
        h3("Project Created By"),
        h2("Jeremy Fyrer & Beri Chavangi"),
        br(),
        h3("Acknowledgements"),
        p(
          "We would like to acknowledge Washington and Lee University 
          for providing the academic environment and resources that 
          made this project possible."
        ),
        p(
          "We also extend our sincere thanks to Professor Ferdous 
          for guidance, instruction, and support throughout this project."
        ),
        br(),
        p(
          style = "font-size:13px; color:#d9e2ed;",
          "Washington and Lee University | Olympic History Data Project"
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TAB 1: COUNTRY MEDALS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tabPanel(
    "Country Medals",

    sidebarLayout(

      sidebarPanel(

        selectInput(
          "season",
          "Select Olympic Season:",
          choices = c("Both", "Summer", "Winter")
        ),

        selectInput(
          "medal_type",
          "Select Medal Type:",
          choices = c("Total", "Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
        ),

        sliderInput(
          "country_number",
          "Number of Countries:",
          min = 5,
          max = 30,
          value = 15
        )
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h3("How many medals does each country have?"),

        plotOutput("country_plot"),
        
        p(
  "This graph displays the number of Olympic medals earned by
  each country, with the results determined by the selected
  season and medal type. The horizontal bars make it possible
  to compare national Olympic success and identify which
  countries have accumulated the most medals. These comparisons
  help illustrate how athletic success has been distributed
  among nations throughout Olympic history.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
),

        tableOutput("country_table")
      )
    )
  ),

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TAB 2: TOP ATHLETES
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tabPanel(
    "Top Athletes",

    sidebarLayout(

      sidebarPanel(

        selectInput(
          "athlete_type",
          "Select Medal Type:",
          choices = c("Total", "Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
        ),

        sliderInput(
          "athlete_number",
          "Number of Athletes:",
          min = 5,
          max = 30,
          value = 10
        )
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h3("Which athletes have the most medals?"),

        plotOutput("athlete_plot"),
        
        p(
  "This graph ranks Olympic athletes according to their total
  number of medals or their gold, silver, or bronze medal
  counts. It highlights the individuals who have achieved
  the greatest success across Olympic competition. Examining
  these athletes provides a look at exceptional individual
  performances and the lasting impact athletes can have
  on Olympic history.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
),

        tableOutput("athlete_table")
      )
    )
  ),

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TAB 3: AGE AND PERFORMANCE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tabPanel(
    "Age & Performance",

    sidebarLayout(

      sidebarPanel(

        selectInput(
          "sport",
          "Select Sport:",
          choices = sort(unique(athletes$Sport))
        ),

        selectInput(
          "age_season",
          "Select Season:",
          choices = c("Both", "Summer", "Winter")
        ),

        selectInput(
          "performance",
          "Select Performance:",
          choices = c(
            "All",
            "Medal winners",
            "Non-medal winners"
          )
        )
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h3("How does age affect performance?"),

        plotOutput("age_plot"),
        
        p(
  "This histogram compares the age distribution of medal-winning
  and non-medal-winning athletes. Age is measured in years, while
  the vertical axis represents the number of athlete-event records
  within each age group. The distribution helps identify the ages
  at which athletes most commonly compete and whether medal
  winners tend to fall within different age ranges. This helps
  investigate the relationship between age and Olympic performance.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
),

        plotOutput("age_boxplot"),

p(
  "This boxplot compares the ages, measured in years, of medal
  winners and athletes who did not earn a medal. The median line
  in each box represents the typical age for each group, while
  the boxes and whiskers show the distribution of ages. Comparing
  these distributions helps determine whether medal-winning
  athletes tend to be younger or older than their competitors.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
)
      )
    )
  ),

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TAB 4: HOSTING ADVANTAGE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tabPanel(
    "Hosting Advantage",

    sidebarLayout(

      sidebarPanel(

        selectInput(
          "host_season",
          "Select Season:",
          choices = c("Both", "Summer", "Winter")
        ),

        selectInput(
          "host_medal",
          "Select Medal Type:",
          choices = c("Total", "Gold")
        )
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h3("Does hosting relate to medal success?"),

        plotOutput("host_plot"),
        
        p(
  "This graph compares the average number of medals earned by
  countries when competing in an Olympic Games they hosted
  versus when competing in other Olympic Games. The vertical
  axis measures average medals per participating country.
  A higher value for home competitions would suggest a possible
  hosting advantage. This comparison helps investigate whether
  competing on home soil is associated with greater Olympic
  success.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
),

        tableOutput("host_table")
      )
    )
  ),
  

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TAB 5: GENDER PARTICIPATION
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tabPanel(
    "Gender Participation",

    sidebarLayout(

      sidebarPanel(

        selectInput(
          "gender_season",
          "Select Season:",
          choices = c("Both", "Summer", "Winter")
        )
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h3("How has participation increased by gender?"),

        plotOutput("gender_plot"),
        
        p(
  "This line graph tracks the number of male and female Olympic
  participants across Olympic years. The horizontal axis
  represents the year of competition, while the vertical axis
  shows the number of individual athletes participating.
  Changes in the lines reveal how participation has evolved
  over time and whether the gap between male and female
  representation has narrowed. This provides important insight
  into the historical expansion of women's participation
  in international sports.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
),

        plotOutput("gender_percentage"),

p(
  "This graph shows the percentage of Olympic participants
  represented by each gender in different Olympic years.
  Unlike the previous graph, which displays the number of
  athletes, this visualization focuses on the proportion
  of total participation. The percentages help show whether
  Olympic representation has become more balanced between
  men and women, regardless of changes in the overall size
  of the Games.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
)
      )
    )
  ),

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TAB 6: COUNTRY TRENDS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tabPanel(
    "Country Trends",

    sidebarLayout(

      sidebarPanel(

        selectizeInput(
          "countries",
          "Select Countries:",
          choices = sort(unique(athletes$Country)),
          selected = NULL,
          multiple = TRUE
        ),

        selectInput(
          "trend_season",
          "Select Season:",
          choices = c("Both", "Summer", "Winter")
        )
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h3("Which countries have improved over time?"),

        plotOutput("trend_plot"),
        
        p(
  "This line graph tracks the number of Olympic medals earned
  by selected countries across different Olympic years.
  The horizontal axis represents the year of competition,
  and the vertical axis represents the number of medals earned.
  Each line represents a different country. Changes in the
  lines reveal periods of national improvement, decline,
  and sustained success. This helps demonstrate how Olympic
  dominance has shifted among countries throughout history.",
  style = "font-size:14px; color:#555; line-height:1.6;"
),

        tableOutput("trend_table")
      )
    )
  )
)

# ============================================================
# 4. SERVER
# ============================================================

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # COUNTRY MEDALS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  country_filtered <- reactive({

    data <- country_summary

    if (input$season != "Both") {
      data <- data %>%
        filter(Season == input$season)
    }

    data %>%
      group_by(Country) %>%
      summarise(
        Gold = sum(Gold),
        Silver = sum(Silver),
        Bronze = sum(Bronze),
        Total = sum(Total),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      arrange(desc(.data[[input$medal_type]]))
  })

  output$country_plot <- renderPlot({

    country_filtered() %>%
      slice_head(n = input$country_number) %>%
      ggplot(
        aes(
          x = reorder(
            Country,
            .data[[input$medal_type]]
          ),
          y = .data[[input$medal_type]]
        )
      ) +
      geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(
        title = "Olympic Medal Rankings",
        x = "Country",
        y = "Number of Medals"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$country_table <- renderTable({

    head(
      country_filtered(),
      input$country_number
    )
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TOP ATHLETES
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  output$athlete_plot <- renderPlot({

    athlete_summary %>%
      arrange(desc(.data[[input$athlete_type]])) %>%
      slice_head(n = input$athlete_number) %>%
      ggplot(
        aes(
          x = reorder(
            Name,
            .data[[input$athlete_type]]
          ),
          y = .data[[input$athlete_type]]
        )
      ) +
      geom_col(fill = "goldenrod") +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(
        title = "Most Decorated Olympic Athletes",
        x = "Athlete",
        y = "Medals"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$athlete_table <- renderTable({

    athlete_summary %>%
      arrange(desc(.data[[input$athlete_type]])) %>%
      head(input$athlete_number)
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # AGE AND PERFORMANCE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  age_filtered <- reactive({

    data <- athletes %>%
      filter(
        Sport == input$sport,
        !is.na(Age)
      )

    if (input$age_season != "Both") {
      data <- data %>%
        filter(Season == input$age_season)
    }

    if (input$performance == "Medal winners") {
      data <- data %>%
        filter(!is.na(Medal))
    }

    if (input$performance == "Non-medal winners") {
      data <- data %>%
        filter(is.na(Medal))
    }

    data
  })

  output$age_plot <- renderPlot({

    age_filtered() %>%
      mutate(
        Performance = if_else(
          is.na(Medal),
          "No medal",
          "Medal winner"
        )
      ) %>%
      ggplot(
        aes(
          x = Age,
          fill = Performance
        )
      ) +
      geom_histogram(
        bins = 25,
        alpha = 0.7,
        position = "identity"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Age Distribution by Performance",
        x = "Age",
        y = "Number of Athlete-Event Records"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$age_boxplot <- renderPlot({

    age_filtered() %>%
      mutate(
        Performance = if_else(
          is.na(Medal),
          "No medal",
          "Medal winner"
        )
      ) %>%
      ggplot(
        aes(
          x = Performance,
          y = Age,
          fill = Performance
        )
      ) +
      geom_boxplot() +
      labs(
        title = "Age Comparison",
        x = "Performance",
        y = "Age"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # HOSTING ADVANTAGE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  game_index <- athletes %>%
  distinct(Games, Year, Season)

participation <- athletes %>%
  distinct(NOC, Games, Season)

# One country label per NOC for display in the host results table.
noc_country <- athletes %>%
  filter(!is.na(Country)) %>%
  distinct(NOC, Country) %>%
  group_by(NOC) %>%
  summarise(Country = first(Country), .groups = "drop")

medal_counts <- medals %>%
  distinct(NOC, Games, Event, Medal) %>%
  group_by(NOC, Games) %>%
  summarise(
    Total = n(),
    Gold = sum(Medal == "Gold"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

  host_data <- reactive({
    games <- host_lookup

    if (input$host_season != "Both") {
      games <- games %>% filter(Season == input$host_season)
    }

    # Attach Year to each Games label using the athlete data.
    # Each Olympic edition is identified by Games + Season.
    host_editions <- participation %>%
      left_join(game_index, by = c("Games", "Season")) %>%
      inner_join(
        games %>% select(Year, Season, Host_NOC, City),
        by = c("Year", "Season")
      )

    # Restrict the comparison to NOCs that have hosted at least once.
    host_countries <- unique(games$Host_NOC)

    comparison <- host_editions %>%
      filter(NOC %in% host_countries) %>%
      left_join(medal_counts, by = c("NOC", "Games")) %>%
      left_join(noc_country, by = "NOC") %>%
      mutate(
        Total = replace_na(Total, 0L),
        Gold = replace_na(Gold, 0L),
        Host_Status = if_else(
          NOC == Host_NOC,
          "Home Olympics",
          "Away Olympics"
        )
      )

    comparison
  })

  output$host_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- host_data()
    metric <- input$host_medal

    validate(
      need(nrow(data) > 0, "No hosting comparison data for this season.")
    )

    plot_data <- data %>%
      group_by(Host_Status) %>%
      summarise(
        Average = mean(.data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )

    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Host_Status, y = Average, fill = Host_Status)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.6) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Home Olympics" = "#D4A017",
          "Away Olympics" = "#3675A9"
        )
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Does Hosting Improve Medal Performance?",
        subtitle = "Average medals won per participating country among past host nations",
        x = "Olympic participation",
        y = paste("Average", tolower(metric), "medals per country"),
        fill = "Location"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
  })

  output$host_table <- renderTable({
    table_data <- host_data() %>%
      filter(NOC == Host_NOC) %>%
      select(Country, NOC, City, Year, Season, Host_Status, Total, Gold) %>%
      arrange(Year)

    validate(
      need(nrow(table_data) > 0, "No host-country results for this season.")
    )

    as.data.frame(table_data)
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # GENDER PARTICIPATION
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  gender_filtered <- reactive({

    data <- gender_data

    if (input$gender_season != "Both") {
      data <- data %>%
        filter(Season == input$gender_season)
    }

    data
  })

  output$gender_plot <- renderPlot({

    ggplot(
      gender_filtered(),
      aes(
        x = Year,
        y = Participants,
        color = Sex
      )
    ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_point() +
      labs(
        title = "Olympic Participation by Gender",
        x = "Year",
        y = "Number of Participants"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$gender_percentage <- renderPlot({

    gender_filtered() %>%
      group_by(Year) %>%
      mutate(
        Percentage = Participants /
          sum(Participants) * 100
      ) %>%
      ggplot(
        aes(
          x = Year,
          y = Percentage,
          color = Sex
        )
      ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      labs(
        title = "Gender Participation Percentage",
        x = "Year",
        y = "Percentage"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # COUNTRY TRENDS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  trend_filtered <- reactive({

    data <- country_trends

    if (input$trend_season != "Both") {
      data <- data %>%
        filter(Season == input$trend_season)
    }

    data %>%
      filter(Country %in% input$countries)
  })

  output$trend_plot <- renderPlot({

    ggplot(
      trend_filtered(),
      aes(
        x = Year,
        y = Medals,
        color = Country
      )
    ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_point() +
      labs(
        title = "Country Medal Performance Over Time",
        x = "Olympic Year",
        y = "Medals"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$trend_table <- renderTable({

    trend_filtered() %>%
      group_by(Country) %>%
      summarise(
        Total_Medals = sum(Medals),
        Best_Performance = max(Medals),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      arrange(desc(Total_Medals))
  })
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 5. RUN SHINY APP
# ============================================================

shinyApp(
  ui = ui,
  server = server
)
```
